articleTitle: A Non-Isolated High Step-Up DC-DC Converter Using Switched-Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: The present paper introduces a novel non-isolated high-gain DC-DC converter. In the new converter, the switched-capacitor (SC) method is utilized to achieve voltage gain. The major aim of the new topology compared with other topologies of the same type is to achieve greater voltage gain with an uncomplicated structure and with minimum voltage stress on semiconductor devices. Additional benefits include constant input current and positive polarity, offering a mutual reference point between the input source and load. Design parameters, semiconductor device voltage stresses, and theoretical analysis are determined when the device is under continuous conduction mode (CCM). PLECS software is lastly used to provide simulation output and verify proposed converter equations.

articleTitle: Magnetic Equivalent Circuit Model for Electromagnetic Analysis of Synchronous Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This paper proposes an accurate magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) model for synchronous reluctance motors (SynRM) which is including the limited number of permeances in air-gap, and iron parts of stator and rotor. In proposed approach, the complex geometry of SynRM is divided into some parts, and the conformal maps are then used to calculate the permeance of relevant part in different paths. The conformal maps such as Schwartz-Christoffel ($\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{C}$) mapping is used to transform the complex geometry of different parts of SynRM into the canonical geometry in rectangle form. The permeance in relavant direction is then easily calculated in canonical geometry. It should be noted that the permeance is maintained while mapping the geometry from the physical domain into the canonical domain. After calculating the linear and non-linear permeances, the non-linear system of equations is created through writing the magnetic equation in different nodes of motor geometry. The newton-Raphson method is then used to solve the system of non-linear equations, to determine the scalar magnetic potential in all magnetic nodes, and to calculate the motor performance. In final, the accuracy of proposed MEC model is verified through comparing with corresponding results obtained from finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: Optimization of Optical Absorber in Plasmonic Detector Structures Using Gratings in NIR
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: The improvement of light absorption is a major change for optical detectors. In this research, a metal-semiconductor-metal photodetector with a patterned metal grating was investigated and the gating was optimized for better light absorption in the near-infrared region. The designed structure consists of a gallium arsenide semiconductor as substrate, a SiO2 layer as insulator and a patterned gold (Au) as metal lattice. The main phenomena for the enhancement of light absorption in this structure are the resonance of the lattice and the propagation of plasmonic waves along the metal contacts and the insulator boundary, as well as the coupling of more light into the semiconductor, which leads to higher carrier generation. The structure with a different number of gratings with fixed grating periodicity (300 nm) was simulated using the finite-difference time-domain method in the Lumerical software. The simulation results show that the maximum absorption occurs in wavelength 840 nm with 8 gratings on each side of the surface of the device.

articleTitle: Combination UFLS and UVLS Aim to Restore Frequency and Voltage Stability Simultaneously
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Microgrids have become a popular technology in recent years due to their environmental compatibility. Microgrids can be operated in two modes: grid-connected and islanded. Due to the integration of this technology with distribution networks, ensuring the correct operation of microgrids is very important. The main challenge in the power grid is the balance between generation and consumption, which must always be under control. In the case of large-scale disturbances in the microgrid, the stability of the system is at risk and if not controlled, it can lead to collapse or even extended blackouts. Load shedding in the microgrid is performed with the aim of curtailing lower priority loads so that the balance between generation and demand is equalized and the stability of the system is maintained and restored. The main objective of this paper is to simultaneously use two important parameters, namely frequency and voltage, to evaluate the state of the network affected by islanding and overload. Using this method, it is possible to simultaneously restore the frequency and voltage in the islanded microgrid within the allowable range. The performance and effectiveness of this method have been simulated and investigated in a 13-bus IEEE network.

articleTitle: Exploring Novel Applications of Electrical Bioimpedance Spectroscopy in Orthopedic Fracture Healing Assessment: Modeling Study
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Bone fracture is a common issue these days and therefore, evaluating the process of healing plays a crucial role in orthopedics. The healing process is usually evaluated by radiography which not only is dangerous but also is time-consuming and costly. This study evaluates the feasibility of using electrical bioimpedance spectroscopy for both bone fracture detection and healing process monitoring in order to overcome the traditional radiography methods' challenges. A biological tissue along with different layers was modelled using COMSOL software. Firstly, the functionality of impedance spectroscopy was assessed for the evaluating the healing process, and then other factors such as the depth of the bone were investigated. Our results have demonstrated that as the bone experiences fractures, the impedance values fall significantly due to the accumulation of fluids, including blood in the fracture site.

articleTitle: Calcium Propionate Detection in Dough Water Using Coplanar Capacitive Sensor: A Practical Investigation
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Calcium propionate, a commonly employed preservative in bread manufacturing, is crucial for preserving food safety and assuring product quality. This study assesses the efficacy of the Coplanar Capacitive Sensor (CCS) in identifying calcium propionate concentrations in dough water (a liquid containing ingredients prepared for mixing with flour). Two different sample types were examined: a deionized solution with varied amounts of calcium propionate and a deionized solution containing baker’s yeast and calcium propionate. The CCS sensor exhibited good sensitivity and linearity across a detection range of 100 to $\mathbf{5 0 0 0} \mathrm{ppm}$ in the first sample type. The inclusion of baker’s yeast in the second sample type lowered the detection range to a maximum of 2500 ppm. Repeatability evaluations indicated a margin of error of $2 \%$, highlighting the sensor’s reliability. These findings demonstrate the viability of coplanarbased capacitive sensors as economical and effective instruments for real-time monitoring of food preservatives while underscoring the impact of sample composition on detection performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Hand Movement Recognition: A Hybrid Fuzzy Deep Neural Network Approach with Time-Frequency EMG Representations
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This study proposes a novel Hybrid Fuzzy Deep Neural Network (HFDNN) for recognizing complex hand movements using electromyography (EMG) signals. The system integrates fuzzy logic for managing uncertainty with deep neural networks (DNNs) for learning spatial and temporal features of EMG signals. Six hand movements, including lifting heavy and light objects, grasping pen-like and card-like objects, making a fist, and opening the hand, were analyzed. EMG signals were preprocessed using a band-pass filter and normalized, followed by feature extraction through short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to generate time-frequency representations as input to the HFDNN. The proposed model achieved a classification accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6. 8 \%}$, with precision, recall, and F1-scores averaging $95.7 \%, 97.2 \%$, and $96.3 \%$, respectively. Compared to traditional CNN, RNN, and hybrid CNN-RNN models, the HFDNN demonstrated superior performance, validated through statistical significance testing ($\mathbf{p}\lt 0.01$). The inclusion of fuzzy rules enhanced decision-making, particularly for overlapping classes. This work underscores the efficacy of hybrid approaches in capturing the intricacies of hand movement signals, paving the way for advancements in prosthetics control and rehabilitation. Comparative analysis with recent studies highlights the proposed method’s robustness and potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: A New Method for DOA Estimation in the Presence of Non-uniform Noise
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of estimating the direction of arrival in non-uniform sensor noise. To this aim, The covariance matrix of the noise is estimated, and its effect is attenuated to obtain an improved covariance matrix of the observations. So, the problem can be solved using common subspace based methods for DOA estimation under uniform white noise assumption like the MUSIC algorithm. Simulation results confirm that the proposed method outperforms other existing subspace based methods when RMSE is utilized as the accuracy metric.

articleTitle: Robust Funnel Based Control of a Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Continuous Stirred Tank Reactors (CSTRs) are essential in chemical processes due to their broad industrial applications and complex nonlinear dynamics, making their control a critical area of study in control theory. This paper tackles the challenge of controlling a CSTR under the influence of disturbances. The funnel control method is introduced as a foundation for robust control, leveraging its strengths in handling nonlinear systems. To further improve performance, a novel control strategy combining funnel control with integral sliding mode is proposed, along with an adaptive law to address parameter uncertainties. Comprehensive simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, highlighting its capability.

articleTitle: A Consumption Optimization Method for Smart Homes Utilizing Backup Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: In modern power grids, the electricity market facilitates two-way communication with smart meters for residential consumers. This capability allows clients to adjust their consumption based on time-of-use (TOU) tariffs and load shedding commands while ensuring their satisfaction. This paper introduces an innovative optimizing method for the home controller, enabling the selection of optimal start times for devices in accordance with TOU signals. It also incorporates strategies to avoid load shedding, all while leveraging a backup battery system to smooth out the load consumption profile. Additionally, the controller utilizes the battery during peak electricity pricing periods to minimize electricity costs. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method effectively reduces both total costs and instances of load shedding.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Experimental Evaluation of the PEDOT:PSS/ZnO Diode Interface
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: ZnO is a seminal wide and direct bandgap semiconductor used in various devices like transparent thin film transistors which require interfacing with other semiconductors and conductors. Particularly, it is prevalent to form devices based on the interfaces between ZnO and organic semiconductors, which are easy to deposit and do not interfere with their transparency. Here, we report the results of our experimental work on the fabrication and assessment of the interface of PEDOT:PSS/ZnO structure. Fabricated devices show strongly asymmetric conductivity, while the I-V characteristics of the device strongly depend on the technique used for the PEDOT:PSS deposition on $\mathbf{Z n O}$ thin films. $\mathbf{Z n O}$ layers are fabricated by sputtering under an oxygen plasma onto a zinc substrate, and PEDOT:PSS/ZnO interface is formed by several techniques of a) drop casting, b) dip coating, and c) flake pressing. In comparison, the devices fabricated using the latter method result in diodes with considerably higher rectification ratio. For the formation of PEDOT:PSS/ZnO contacts with almost symmetric conductivity, drop casting appears to be more promising.

articleTitle: Emission Reduction for a Home in Iraq Utilizing Geothermal System Supplied by Isolated Photovoltaic-Wind-Diesel Generator Using Genetic Algorithm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: The main goal of this article is to focus on reducing the effect of emissions for a home located in a remote area in Iraq supplied by an isolated Photovoltaic (PV), Wind Turbine (WT), with a backup system containing Battery Storage System (BSS), and Diesel Generator (DG), the new addition used in this article is a Geothermal System (GS). Using GS as an additional tool that will affect the cooling load’s power consumption by making useful underground temperature, will minimize the total power consumption by saving the generating power energy. The proposed model is simulated using a Genetic Algorithm (GA) for a home in Basrah City, Southern region of Iraq, the results illustrate the difference in the emission value with and without using GS. It shows that the power drawn from DG is reduced when turning on the cooling load, meaning less emission.

articleTitle: A Low-Loss and Low-Dispersion Photonic Crystal Fiber for Optical Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: In this paper, to reduce the loss and dispersion of photonic crystal fibers, a design consisting of six layers of holes is presented. The radius of the air holes varies from 0.21 to 0.7 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ from the core outwards. The refractive index of 1.41 obtained from simulation and the spatial distribution function of the electric field intensity in the core shows that proper confinement occurred in the fiber and a loss of $3.34 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~dB}. \mathrm{cm}^{-}$<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> for a wavelength of 1550 nm confirmed this. The dispersion value of $0.026 \mathrm{ps}. \mathrm{nm}^{-1} \cdot \mathrm{~km}^{-1}$ at the mentioned wavelength showed that the proposed design performs better compared to recent research. The effective surface area in this case equals $7.93 \mu \mathrm{~m}^{2}$. The use of circular holes in the designed structure helps simplify the fabrication process.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Damped Sinusoidal Signal Based on Linear Prediction Method
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This paper presents, a novel method for estimating the damping factor and frequency of real-valued damped Sinusoidal signals. The proposed approach models the damping factor and frequency using the coefficients of an autoregressive (AR) model, estimated through the Generalized Eigenvalue Problem (GEP) method. Evaluation results demonstrate the method’s superior performance, particularly in terms of Mean Squared Error (MSE) across a wide frequency range. Notably, at both low and high frequencies, the proposed method exhibits significantly lower MSE values, implying that proposed method consistently outperforms in overall reliability and robustness for damping factor and frequency estimation.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on the Applications of High-Entropy Alloys in Electronics and Energy Industries
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), characterized by their unique multi-element composition in near-equal proportions, have garnered significant attention for their remarkable mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and thermal stability. These properties enable HEAs to address critical challenges in the electronics and energy industries. In electronics, HEAs offer customizable electrical conductivity, low melting points, and exceptional durability, making them ideal for applications in semiconductors, flexible electronics, and advanced packaging. Similarly, in the energy sector, HEAs demonstrate superior performance in hydrogen storage, electrochemical reactions, and thermal management, supporting the development of next-generation clean energy technologies. However, widespread adoption of HEAs is hindered by challenges such as phase instability, fabrication complexities, and brittleness at low temperatures. This paper provides a comprehensive review of HEA research, emphasizing innovative solutions such as computational design and nanostructuring to overcome these barriers. By examining their transformative potential and addressing the obstacles to their integration, this study highlights the pivotal role of HEAs in shaping advanced technologies for sustainable and high-performance systems.

articleTitle: Detection of Hand Movement Using Time, Frequency and Time-Frequency Features of the Electromyogram Signal in Order to Create a Human-Machine Interface
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This study presents an electromyography (EMG)-based hand gesture recognition system that leverages machine learning techniques to accurately classify hand gestures. A total of 33 participants (21 men and 12 women, average age 24.8 years) performed six hand movements under controlled conditions. EMG signals were recorded at a sampling rate of 1024 Hz and filtered using a band-pass Butterworth filter (20–450 Hz) and a notch filter to remove power-line interference. Signal normalization ensured consistency across trials, and extensive feature extraction was conducted, capturing time-domain, frequency-domain, time-frequency, and nonlinear characteristics. To optimize classification, three feature selection methods were employed: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), and Mutual Information (MI). Results indicate that MI-based feature selection, coupled with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier, provided the highest accuracy ($\mathbf{9 1 . 7 \%}$) across key metrics, outperforming linear SVM. This study highlights the importance of signal preprocessing, feature extraction, and appropriate classifier selection for enhancing the robustness of EMG-based gesture recognition. The findings have potential applications in prosthetics, assistive technology, and human-machine interfaces (HMIs), offering a reliable approach for interpreting complex EMG signals.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Fuzzy-Tuned PID and Optimal Frequency Control for Hybrid Resonant Three-Level ZCS Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive fuzzy-tuned PID control strategy for regulating the output voltage of hybrid multilevel zero current switching (ZCS) DC-DC converters. The approach focuses on controlling switches in the auxiliary circuit while maintaining a fixed $50 \%$ duty cycle in the main circuit. By integrating fuzzy logic with traditional PID control, the fuzzy gain scheduling (FGS) PID controller dynamically adjusts PID coefficients in response to varying operational conditions, enhancing control performance. Furthermore, optimal control of switching frequency mitigates current stresses on the resonant tank during startup and short circuit events, adapting frequency based on output voltage levels. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional PID and fuzzy logic controllers by reducing overshoots, achieving quicker settling times, and effectively managing current stresses during transient and fault conditions, ensuring safe converter operation.

articleTitle: Flexible PEDOT:PSS/PVA Temperature Sensor for Cost-Effective Wearable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: The development of flexible and biocompatible temperature sensors is critical for wearable healthcare applications, enabling continuous and non-invasive body temperature monitoring. This paper presents a temperature sensor based on a PEDOT:PSS/PVA composite fabricated using a straightforward drop-casting method encapsulated with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) for enhanced durability and biocompatibility. The device is based on the negative temperature coefficient (NTC) charateristics of the fabricated composite polymer, facilitating accurate measurement of temperature alterations. The fabricated sensor demonstrates consistent performance across a physiological temperature range $\left(32^{\circ} \mathrm{C}-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$, achieving a temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) of $0.68 \%{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Measurements show a stable decrease in resistance when the sensor is in touch with human skin, reflecting its sensitivity to skin temperature changes. Experimental results show that the resistance returned to its initial baseline; highlighting the repeatability of the sensor and its reliability for dynamic monitoring. The encapsulation with PDMS further enhances the flexibility of the sensor and protects it against environmental hazards while maintaining its electrical and mechanical performance intact. Compared to existing flexible temperature sensors, this device offers a practical balance of sensitivity, flexibility, and ease of fabrication. Its simple design and scalable fabrication make it suitable for various wearable medical applications, including fever detection, thermal mapping, and integration into advanced health monitoring IoT systems. This study contributes to the advancement of flexible electronics for personalized healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Bioimpedance Sensor for Measuring the Electrical Properties of Blood in the Hemodialysis Process
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This study presents the design and simulation of a bioimpedance sensor aimed at measuring the electrical properties of blood during the hemodialysis process. Utilizing two configurations—4-electrode washer and Van der Pauw—the simulations were conducted in the COMSOL environment using the finite element method. Performance accuracy was evaluated against data from Gabriel et al., with results analyzed in MATLAB, including Nyquist curve examination under various conditions. The findings indicate that for the 4-electrode washer method, optimal sensor performance occurs when the current injection radius matches the voltage reading radius; however, this configuration presents construction challenges. Conversely, the 4-electrode Van der Pauw method demonstrated that the radius of the electrodes significantly impacts sensor evaluation and performance. By optimizing electrode dimensions, a compact sensor design can be developed, potentially enhancing the quality of dialysis machines and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting Using Multilayer Neural Networks: A Residential Complex Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Short-term electric load forecasting (STLF) is a crucial tool for optimizing energy consumption and load management in power systems. This study aims to develop an accurate short-term electric load forecasting model using multilayer neural networks (MLNNs) that integrates historical electrical load data with meteorological variables. The dataset used for training the model was collected from a residential complex in Ahvaz, Iran, spanning from March 21, 2021, to August 24, 2021. It includes $\mathbf{7, 2 2 2}$ records of half-hourly electrical load data, along with the corresponding weather data such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and atmospheric pressure. The primary objective of the model is to improve the prediction accuracy for energy consumption in dynamic environments, such as large buildings or industrial complexes, where various internal and external factors influence electricity demand. The results revealed that the model performed exceptionally well on the first day, with the forecasted loads closely aligning with the actual loads and minimal deviation. However, as the forecasting period extended, the accuracy gradually declined, especially in high-demand scenarios. Specifically, over the seven-day period, the forecasted loads were approximately $6.5 \%$ higher than the actual loads. Despite these discrepancies, the model effectively captured the overall trend of electricity demand, providing valuable insights for energy management and grid optimization. Overall, while the model’s performance can be enhanced, it provides a solid foundation for improving short-term electric load forecasting and serves as a valuable tool for demand-side management and energy efficiency strategies.

articleTitle: One-bit DOA Estimation with Array Imperfections: A Learning-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Low-power and low-complexity Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation is a critical challenge in various signal processing applications. This paper presents a data-driven approach using a neural network framework designed for single-snapshot, one-bit quantized measurements, enabling significant hardware simplification. We explore a Fully Connected (FC) Neural Network architecture (which is identical to a 1D convolutional architecture in the single-snapshot case) trained end-to-end on raw quantized data. The performance of this learned approach is rigorously compared against the well-established MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) and Complex-valued Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding (CBIHT) algorithms. Our findings reveal that the proposed neural network achieves superior estimation performance compared to these, especially under low SNR values and in the presence of realistic array imperfections. We observe significant performance gains even without explicitly training the network on data with such imperfections, highlighting the generalization capabilities of the proposed method.

articleTitle: PID Controller Design for a Mechatronic System using Lion Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Controllers act as a bridge between the operator and the system, allowing the operator to communicate with the system as if it were a human. In other words, the controller is like the thinking brain of an industrial process. A controller communicates all the commands that an expert wants to apply to the system to follow its standard flow process and ultimately achieve the desired response. When industrial processes are left alone and without a controller in the control loop, they typically do not give satisfactory responses in terms of transient or steady-state characteristics. Therefore, the selection and programming of an appropriate controller is one of the most important steps in an industrial process. One of the most widely used and well-known controllers is the PID controller, whose gains are often determined experimentally or through trial and error. However, finding the optimal gains is always a challenge. In this study, for the first time, the optimal gains of the PID controller are determined using Lion Optimization Algorithm (LOA). This research has introduced a systematic and efficient approach to achieving optimal control of mechatronic systems.

articleTitle: Separating Harmonic Contribution of Load and Power Distribution Network of Ahvaz at the Point of Common Coupling Using Correlation Analysis on Measured Currents and Voltages
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Nowadays, the topic of harmonics is one of the crucial subjects in assessing the power quality of electrical networks. Harmonics are recognized as the most significant power quality disturbance in the network. Non-linear loads and distributed generation sources, such as inverter-based solar cells, which play an undeniable role in distribution networks with the advancement of renewable energies, cause the expansion of network harmonics. Identifying voltage and current harmonic distortions and determining the sources of voltage imbalance are among the most critical challenges in power systems. Today, the evaluation of power quality has gained increasing importance mainly due to the widespread use of non-linear electronic devices and variable non-linear loads in network equipment and on the consumer side. Therefore, determining the factor causing harmonic disturbance and its contribution to this disturbance is necessary. In this paper, firstly, the harmonic model of specified loads is developed, and subsequently, the harmonic contribution of the load and the network at the common coupling point is determined through the measurement of current and voltage at the load-network connection point.

articleTitle: Blood Pressure Regulation Using a FOPID Controller Based on a Hybrid-Evolutionary Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: In recent years, due to the strong need to control blood pressure in patients, especially patients with heart problems, several control structures have been designed and implemented to control their blood pressure. The reason for this is the instability of blood pressure in this group of patients, and nurses and doctors need to use methods to prevent this instability, which can be a fatal factor for patients. To achieve this goal, a fractional-order PID controller whose coefficients are calculated using a hybrid-evolutionary algorithm called BH-PSO has been used in this paper. This control combination can excessively improve the system’s output response. This control structure can significantly reduce the error rate and settling time. Also, for the objective function, three functions integral absolute error (IAE), integral squared error (ISE), and integral time absolute error (ITAE) have been used to compare and reduce the system’s error rate.

articleTitle: Real-Time Occlusion-Aware Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for real-time object tracking in occlusion-prone environments, addressing critical challenges in achieving robustness, accuracy, and efficiency under dynamic and cluttered conditions. The proposed system integrates geometric analysis using Intersection over Union (IoU), probabilistic validation via a Hidden Markov Model (HMM), and an advanced object detection module to ensure consistent performance during both partial and complete occlusions. Evaluated on the KITTI dataset, the system achieves a Success Rate of $\mathbf{8 3 \%}$, Precision of $\mathbf{9 3 \%}$, Recall of $\mathbf{8 6 \%}$, and an F1 Score of 0.91, outperforming state-of-the-art methods such as Query-Guided Redetection Tracker (QRDT) and Siamese Occlusion-Aware Network (SiamON) in terms of accuracy and reaction time, with a low processing delay of 35 ms. While QRDT and SiamON offer competitive results, the proposed system demonstrates superior resilience to prolonged occlusions and enhanced suitability for time-critical applications like autonomous driving and surveillance. Limitations related to identity consistency during extended occlusions are acknowledged, with future directions focused on incorporating advanced trajectory prediction and multi-modal sensor fusion. This research establishes a robust foundation for occlusion-aware tracking and contributes significantly to the domains of autonomous systems, robotics, and computer vision

articleTitle: Attention-Based Segmentation of Brain Tumors Using Feature Level Fusion and UNet Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: In medical image analysis, brain tumor segmentation is a crucial step in precise brain tumor diagnosis, treatment planning, and tumor monitoring. In this study, we introduce FusedD2AResNeXtUNet, a novel segmentation method for brain tumor segmentation that incorporates a fusion-attention mechanism. This approach leverages advanced fusion techniques to combine multi-level features, enhancing the model’s focus on the most relevant features and improving the accuracy and robustness of tumor segmentation. By addressing challenges such as variability in tumor shape and size, the fusion mechanism ensures more precise and reliable outcomes. We evaluate our method using the BraTS2020 dataset, a benchmark dataset in the field. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in segmentation performance, including better sensitivity, fewer false positives, high pixel-wise accuracy, reduced pixel-wise error, and increased Dice accuracy. The proposed method achieves a Mean Dice of $\mathbf{9 0. 0 \%}$ on test images, outperforming conventional segmentation techniques. These findings highlight the potential of our fusionenhanced method as a valuable tool for clinical applications in brain tumor diagnosis and treatment planning.

articleTitle: Optimizing Relay Protection in Distributed Generation Systems Through Intelligent Electronic Devices Powered by Current Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: The integration of Distributed Generation (DG) systems, particularly wind turbine generators (WTGs), into power grids presents significant challenges in protection and coordination due to their unique characteristics. Traditional protection methods, such as overcurrent protection, are often insufficient for generator systems with limited short-circuit current contributions. This paper explores the limitations of conventional relay protection for wind turbines, highlighting issues such as reverse power flow, false tripping, and inadequate selectivity. We propose a solution involving Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) powered by current transformers (CTs) to improve protection functionality, adapt to changing network conditions, and enhance system reliability. The paper further discusses the advantages of IEDs, such as adaptive fault detection, real-time monitoring, and reduced downtime. We present an evaluation of various protection functions for wind turbines, including phase overcurrent, neutral overcurrent, and voltage-based protection, as well as the integration of IEDs with modern protection schemes. Finally, the feasibility of implementing CT-powered IEDs in a distribution network model is examined using the ETAP software suite, offering insights into their performance and impact on DG systems.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization using RSSI based Supervised Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Wireless indoor localization has attracted significant interest from industrial and academic domains due to its crucial role in location-based applications. However, localization is not an inherent feature of the ZigBee devices; it is possible to employ wireless technology capabilities for localization. This paper uses machine learning models to map the indoor localization system between the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) and the node position. A system map is created using a fingerprint technique containing an RSSI (input)position(output) pair. To study the influence of RSSI on the localization algorithm, we proposed framework employs four different Supervised Machine Learning models, including K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Feed-Forward Neural Network (FF), Cascade-Forward Neural Network (CF), and Long-Short - Term Memory-Recurrent Neural Network (LSTM-RNN). The results showed that $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ technology achieved the best performance in the CF model over all.

articleTitle: Robust WCET Estimation via Ensemble Learning with Fractional-Order Legendre Function Kernels
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Estimating Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET) as a regression problem has become increasingly challenging due to the complexity of modern hardware and software systems. Traditional statistical methods often fall short of providing accurate and reliable estimates. To address these limitations, ensemble learning methods have emerged as a promising approach for capturing edge cases in execution scenarios. This paper proposes a novel ensemble model that integrates fractional-order Legendre functions (FLF) to enrich feature representation. This integration reduces correlations between individual models within the ensemble, enhancing generalization capabilities. Our method achieves significant reductions in Mean Squared Error (MSE) for WCET estimates while maintaining high levels of safeness. Specifically, the proposed model maintained an error below one across most benchmarks, with safeness levels of $\% 100$ in 13 out of 16 benchmarks. These findings underscore the efficacy of our approach and its potential to provide robust and accurate WCET estimates for complex systems.

articleTitle: Flexible Improvement in Distribution Network Under Intelligent Automation System
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Error management processes encompass the detection, localization, and isolation of faults to ensure the continuous service of the healthy sections of the network. Automating these processes significantly reduces downtime duration. Perhaps the most critical incentive for distribution companies to implement automation is its substantial impact on enhancing system resilience and reliability. Network resilience is one of the primary goals of smart grid implementation and distribution network automation. This paper investigates the effect of installing automatic switching devices (distribution feeder automation) on improving the resilience of distribution networks during fault and failure conditions. To this end, several indices and scenarios regarding the number, type, and location of automatic and non-automatic switches for implementing feeder automation are introduced to evaluate the resilience of the distribution system. Additionally, a modified version of the particle swarm optimization algorithm is presented to determine the optimal placement of switching devices in the presence of distributed generation sources at the distribution levels. As a result, the possibility of islanding predetermined sections during fault conditions is created, reducing customer outages and improving network resilience. It is noteworthy that loads are prioritized based on their importance, so in the event of a fault, maintaining the supply to critical loads is given greater emphasis. This means that the resilience assessment is conducted with a focus on essential loads.

articleTitle: Architecture of AC-DC Energy Nodes in Supergrids: A Technical Foundation for Future Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: The AC-DC Energy Nodes (ADENs) concept offers a transformative approach to modernizing power grids, particularly in the context of supergrids. By centralizing power flows from diverse renewable energy sources, such as offshore wind farms, ADENs enable efficient long-distance power transmission through HVDC technology. This design enhances the balance of supply and demand across regions and countries, significantly improving grid stability and resilience. However, the implementation of ADENs presents substantial technical, regulatory, and cybersecurity challenges. This study delves into these challenges while also addressing the geopolitical complexities of transnational connections, underscoring the critical importance of policy alignment for successful deployment.

articleTitle: A Review on Energy Efficiency in Software-Defined Wireless Sensor Networks for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) transforms the structure of our globalized society there is an urgent need for energy-efficient and reconfigurable network solutions. In this paper, we explore the software-defined wireless sensor networks (SDWSNs), with energy being one of the key driving forces that can greatly augment the network functioning whilst prolonging the life of sensor nodes in various application domains of IoT. The most current approaches that employ advanced developments towards energy efficiency, namely intelligent data aggregation and balancing techniques, sleep scheduling strategies, and routing protocols, were reviewed in this study. It also identifies significant ongoing issues and future research directions and addresses energy efficiency issues by synthesizing ideas from various studies. This survey provides excellent information about technology and insight that derives from the current state of methods and challenges for primary concern to scientific and industrial communities and professional stakeholders regarding SDWSNs.

articleTitle: Entropy-Driven Data Reduction for Nonlinear System Identification Using ANFIS
publicationTitle: 2025 Fifth National and the First International Conference on Applied Research in Electrical Engineering (AREE)
abstract: Intelligent systems theory embraces uncertainty as an intrinsic feature of information and tries to address problems adaptively without forcing them into some predefined formula. Instead, the theory examines systems based on their inherent characteristics, uncovering knowledge that is usually represented in data sets. While volume grows, processing time increases rapidly; the challenge is in how modern methods detect redundancy in the datasets and arrive at a reduced yet effective subset of data. This paper deals with the aforementioned challenge. We propose a methodology that combines knowledge granulation, defined using Yager’s fuzzy entropy, with the ANFIS framework to validate the effectiveness of the reduced data subset in maintaining high performance with reduced computational overhead in system identification through the core input-output relationships of the dataset. The proposed method enables faster and more efficient knowledge extraction by alleviating redundancy compared to traditional techniques. As for demonstration of the effectiveness of it, the ANFIS methodology is applied to the so-called family of commonly met arbitrary function estimation problems. Through simulation results, this new approach confirms the effective preservation of the approximation capability on identifying nonlinear systems while seriously relaxing computational costs.
